He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and considered one of the top players in his class at Dream City Christian School in [[Glendale, Arizona]]. Sharpe signed with [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] but did not play a [[college basketball|college]] game before entering the [[2022 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Sharpe played basketball for [[H. B. Beal Secondary School]] in his hometown of [[London, Ontario]] and led his team to the [[Ontario Federation of School Athletic Associations]] AAA title.{{cite web |last1=Silva |first1=Edilson J. |title=Canadian Stud Shaedon Sharpe blowing-up the spot |url=https://basketballbuzz.ca/hs/aau/canadian-stud-shaedon-sharpe-blowing-up-the-spot |website=BasketballBuzz |access-date=September 5, 2021 |date=July 19, 2021}} He moved to Sunrise Christian Academy in [[Bel Aire, Kansas]], where he had a limited production as a sophomore.{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=Shaedon Sharpe’s Stock Continues to Ascend with Monster Start to the Season |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/shaedon-sharpe-canada-dream-city-chrisitan-recruiting-duke-kenticky-oregon |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=September 5, 2021 |date=November 23, 2020}} For his junior season, Sharpe transferred to Dream City Christian School in [[Glendale, Arizona]] and assumed a leading role.{{cite web |last1=Scott |first1=Dana |title=4-star Canadian recruit Shaedon Sharpe joins Dream City Christian boys basketball team |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/07/28/dream-city-christian-boys-basketball-lands-top-recruit-shaedon-sharpe/5523593002/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=September 5, 2021 |date=July 28, 2020}} He averaged 21.4 points and six rebounds per game in the Grind Session.{{cite web |last1=Pascoe |first1=Bruce |title=Four-star 2022 guard Shaedon Shape of Canada taking unofficial visit to Arizona |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/four-star-2022-guard-shaedon-shape-of-canada-taking-unofficial-visit-to-arizona/article_43ca4700-d46b-11eb-b58a-97bda2f258ab.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=September 5, 2021 |date=June 23, 2021}} He competed for UPLAY Canada on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit, with whom he was mentored by Dwayne Washington.{{cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Ryan |title=What's Next: Shaedon Sharpe Was Barely Ranked Last Year—Now He’s Ready to Take Over at Kentucky |url=https://www.slamonline.com/the-magazine/shaedon-sharpe-ready-to-take-over-at-kentucky/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |access-date=June 20, 2022 |date=November 30, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Sharpe was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and was ranked as the third-best player in the 2021 class by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].{{cite web |title=Shaedon Sharpe, Dream City Christian, Shooting Guard |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Shaedon-Sharpe-46097657/high-school-245657/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=June 20, 2022}}{{cite web |title=Shaedon Sharpe, 2021 Shooting guard |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2021/shaedon-sharpe-257731 |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=June 20, 2022}} He was previously the number one player in the 2022 class before reclassifying.{{cite web |last1=Bossi |first1=Eric |title=Shaedon Sharpe claims the No. 1 spot in updated 2022 rankings |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/LongFormArticle/Shaedon-Sharpe-claims-the-No-1-spot-in-247Sports-updated-2022-rankings-170990475/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=June 20, 2022 |date=September 15, 2021}} Sharpe was unranked by major recruiting services early in his high school career and became one of the top players in his class in about one year, in part due to his success at the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] in 2021.{{cite web |last1=O'Donnell |first1=Ricky |title=Shaedon Sharpe is the NBA Draft mystery box with all of the tools and none of the tape |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2022/6/16/23165686/shaedon-sharpe-scouting-report-nba-draft-2022-highlights-stats |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=June 20, 2022 |date=June 16, 2022}} On September 7, 2021, he committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] over offers from [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]] and the [[NBA G League Ignite]]. He was the first number one recruit to commit to the program since [[Nerlens Noel]] in 2012.{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Shaedon Sharpe, top-ranked prospect in class of 2022, commits to Kentucky Wildcats |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32167191/shaedon-sharpe-top-ranked-prospect-class-2022-commits-kentucky-wildcats |access-date=September 8, 2022 | bball = yes }} == College career == Sharpe graduated early from high school with the intention of [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his first year at Kentucky and playing in the [[2022–23 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2022–23 season]].{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=No. 1 men's basketball prospect Shaedon Sharpe to enroll early with Kentucky Wildcats, won't play until 2022-23 season |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32591108/no-1-prospect-shaedon-sharpe-enroll-early-kentucky-wildcats-play-2022-23-season |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=June 20, 2022 |date=November 9, 2021}} On February 7, 2022, head coach [[John Calipari]] announced that Sharpe would not play for the team in the [[2021–22 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2021–22 season]] after speculation that he would play and enter the [[2022 NBA draft]], for which he was eligible.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Kentucky star freshman Shaedon Sharpe won't play this season, John Calipari says |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33237716/kentucky-star-freshman-shaedon-sharpe-play-season-says-john-calipari |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=June 20, 2022 |date=February 7, 2022}} On April 21, Sharpe declared for the 2022 draft, forgoing his remaining college eligibility without playing a game.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Shaedon Sharpe, who never played for Kentucky as a freshman, to enter 2022 NBA draft, sources say |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33778766/shaedon-sharpe-never-played-kentucky-freshman-enter-2022-nba-draft-sources-say |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=June 20, 2022 |date=April 21, 2022}} ==National team career== Sharpe represented Canada at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in Brazil. He averaged 13 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 2.3 assists, helping his team win the silver medal.{{cite web |last1=Vaught |first1=Larry |title=UK recruiting target Shaedon Sharpe has goals he pursues every day |url=https://www.yoursportsedge.com/2021/02/16/uk-recruiting-target-shaedon-sharpe-has-goals-he-pursues-every-day/vaughts-views/larryvaught/ |website=Your Sports Edge |access-date=September 5, 2021 |date=February 16, 2021}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://ukathletics.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/shaedon-sharpe/9486 Kentucky Wildcats bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Sharpe, Shaedon}} [[Category:2003 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Canadian men's basketball players]] [[Category:Canadian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Sportspeople from London, Ontario]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Basketball people from Ontario]]
